body.title: Will FaZe win a Tier 1 event in 2026?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if FaZe Clan's CS2 roster wins (takes 1st place in) any Tier 1 CS2 tournament that concludes by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "Tier 1 Event" refers to any tournament classified as S-Tier on Liquipedia.net. Online-only events, or events downgraded prior to event start (e.g., downgraded to A-Tier due to team attendance) do not qualify. If a Tier 1 event is downgraded after it has concluded, this event will still qualify as a "Tier 1 Event". 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizers (e.g., ESL, PGL, BLAST.tv, etc.).

body.title: Will Valve add sticker trade-ups before November?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Valve adds sticker trade-ups to Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For the purposes of this market, "sticker trade-ups" is defined as an officially supported in-game mechanic that allows players to combine or exchange multiple stickers to receive a higher-tier sticker. The feature must be fully implemented and accessible to all players in the live game client.

If the feature is added as a limited-time, temporary, or beta mechanic that is reversed or removed within 48 hours of its introduction, this market will resolve to "No." This market will remain open for 48 hours after a qualifying feature is released.

For the purpose of this market, "Valve" refers to Valve Corporation, the developer and publisher of the Counter-Strike series.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Valve; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

body.title: Will CS2 Add a Shootout OT by December 31?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Valve officially implements a shootout-based overtime format for Premier mode in Counter-Strike 2 on or before December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying implementation is an official Valve update that adds, to Premier mode, a tie-breaking format in which a 15:15 tie is resolved through a series of 1v1 shootout arenas, as documented in Valve's official patch notes or update announcements. The implemented format must substantially match the concept of players facing off in 1v1 arenas with the match decided by winning a majority of those arenas. Minor differences in the exact number of arenas, the matchmaking of players within them, or the win threshold will not prevent a "Yes" resolution, provided a 1v1 shootout tie-breaker is officially added to Premier.

A proposal, teaser, survey, or statement of intent that is not accompanied by the format actually going live in Premier will not count. Unofficial modifications, third-party or tournament-specific rule sets, community server configurations, and datamined or unreleased changes that are not part of a published official update will not count.

The primary resolution source will be Valve's official Counter-Strike 2 patch notes and update announcements, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

body.title: Will ArrowCS eat a bug on stream by December 31?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ArrowCS eats a bug during any livestreams between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Eating a bug" refers to ArrowCS placing any part of the body of an insect or other arthropod (such as a cricket, ant, beetle, or similar) into his mouth and closing his mouth during a live broadcast.

A qualifying bug may be alive, dead, cooked, raw, or otherwise prepared provided it is a recognizable part of the body of an insect or other arthropod.

The relevant part of the body of an insect or other arthropod must be a discrete item and retain its original physical form. Processed or insect-derived products, such as insect flour, protein bars, or snacks containing ground insects, will not count. 

ArrowCS must close his mouth with the relevant bug inside, defined as his two lips being completely shut. Merely holding, licking, or placing a bug in the mouth without closure will not count. If he later removes the bug from his mouth after a qualifying action, that will have no bearing on resolution of this market.

The full act as described above must be clearly broadcast on a livestream to qualify. Pre-recorded or edited footage that is not part of a live broadcast will not count.

The resolution source for this market will be qualifying livestream footage.

body.title: Will ropz Get Pulled Over Again in 2026?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robin "ropz" Kool is pulled over by law enforcement between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying stop occurs when law enforcement officers in any jurisdiction signal or direct a motor vehicle driven by ropz to stop, regardless of the reason for the stop and regardless of whether it results in a fine, a warning, or no penalty. 

Stops at fixed checkpoints or border crossings, stops of vehicles in which ropz is a passenger rather than the driver will not count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

A qualifying stop must be publicly confirmed to have occurred. Confirmation may come from a statement or footage published by ropz, from an official law enforcement statement, or from credible reporting. A statement by ropz will qualify only if it explicitly describes a stop that actually occurred; jokes, memes, or hypothetical references will not qualify.

If a qualifying stop occurs within the window, this market will resolve to "Yes" once it is publicly confirmed. A qualifying stop that is not publicly confirmed by January 14, 2027, 11:59 PM ET will not qualify, and if no qualifying stop has been confirmed by that time this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be public statements from ropz and/or local, state, or federal law enforcement; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

body.title: Will FalleN Win an S-Tier Event in 2026?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Gabriel "FalleN" Toledo wins an S-Tier Counter-Strike event between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An S-Tier event means a Counter-Strike tournament classified as S-Tier by the Liquipedia Counter-Strike wiki (https://liquipedia.net/counterstrike/S-Tier_Tournaments) at the time the tournament concludes. A later change to a tournament's Liquipedia tier classification will not affect this market.

Winning means being a member of the winning team's lineup at that event and having played in at least one map for that team during the event. Appearances in a non-playing role, for example as a coach or an unused substitute, will not qualify. The match or standing that decides the event title must conclude within the window above.

If it cannot be determined whether FalleN won a qualifying event by January 14, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the relevant tournament organizers and HLTV.org, with tier classification per Liquipedia; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

body.title: Will Valve add Cobblestone to the map pool by...?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Valve adds the map Cobblestone to the official map pool by the listed date at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the listed market will resolve to "No".

If Cobblestone is added to the Active Duty pool, it must remain there continuously for at least 48 hours for the relevant market to resolve to "Yes". Temporary additions (e.g., for testing) that are reversed within 48 hours will not count. If Cobblestone is added after the deadline, the relevant market will resolve to "No", even if the addition was announced earlier.

For the purpose of this market, "Valve" refers to Valve Corporation, the developer and publisher of the Counter-Strike series.

For the purpose of this market, the "official map pool" refers to the Active Duty map group in Counter-Strike 2 (CS2), which consists of the maps eligible for both competitive matchmaking and professional tournaments.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Valve; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
